The branch current sensor is an independent safety input. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command. The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator.

The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector.

content.content:
1	Sites that install several electric-vehicle charging connectors frequently supply those connectors from a single electrical branch. The branch is protected at an allowable aggregate current, referred to herein as a branch limit, that is commonly lower than the sum of the individual connector ratings. Installing a branch large enough for every connector to draw its full rating at the same time is often impractical, because the cost of the additional service capacity, conductors, and protective devices can exceed the cost of the charging equipment itself.
2	
3	Charging equipment therefore has to share a fixed amount of current among connectors that could collectively demand more. The signalling mechanism ordinarily available for that purpose is the control pilot presented to each vehicle, which advertises a maximum current that the vehicle is permitted to draw. Control-pilot signalling is advisory in nature. The value advertised on the pilot is a command, not a measurement, and the current actually drawn depends on the behaviour of the vehicle receiving it. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous value while its own thermal or state-of-charge logic settles, or may not reduce at all. Control that assumes the commanded value is the delivered value therefore has no way to detect the case in which the branch remains loaded above its limit after a reduction has been ordered, and that case is precisely the one in which the branch protective device is at risk of operating and removing service from every connector on the branch.
4	
5	A further difficulty arises because the branch usually carries loads other than charging. Lighting, building services, and other equipment on the same branch consume part of the allowable aggregate current, and that consumption varies through the day. Allocation that divides the full branch limit among the connectors, without accounting for the varying non-charging portion of the branch load, either overcommits the branch or forces the installer to configure a permanently conservative limit that wastes capacity for most of the day.
6	
7	Sharing schemes that divide available current equally, or in proportion to instantaneous request, also tend to treat every session alike. Where sessions have been served unequally over the course of a shared-capacity period, for example because one session began while the branch was heavily loaded and another began while it was lightly loaded, equal division perpetuates the inequality rather than correcting it.
8	
9	Charging equipment is additionally exposed to conditions that are specific to its power path and its installation. A contactor whose contacts have welded continues to pass current after an open command has been issued, so an allocation scheme that treats an open command as removal of the load will continue to believe that capacity has been released when it has not. Site communication to a remote management system is not continuous, so equipment that depends on a remote authority for both authorization and current limits either stops serving vehicles when the link fails or continues without a governing limit. Multi-connector equipment is also wired by hand, and a transposition between the logical identifier of a connector and the physical contactor and sensor channel that serve it causes a current limit intended for one connector to be applied to another, which defeats the allocation entirely while leaving every individual component apparently functional.
10	
11	There remains a need for charging control that treats the current actually present on the branch and at each connector as the governing quantity, that keeps the branch within its limit even when a vehicle does not honour a reduced pilot command, that allocates the genuinely available portion of the branch limit in a way that corrects accumulated inequality between sessions, and that remains safe and operable when the site link is down, when a contactor has welded, and when the installation wiring map has not been independently confirmed.
12

1	In the following description, reference is made to the accompanying drawings, which form a part of this disclosure and show particular embodiments by way of illustration. Other embodiments may be used and structural or logical changes may be made without departing from the scope of the disclosure. Like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views.
2	
3	Overview of the system
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a charging control system in which an edge controller 100 manages charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the plurality of connectors from a single point of protection. The allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, referred to in this description as the branch limit, is lower than the sum of the ratings of the connectors that the branch conductor 102 supplies. The branch limit is a stored value that corresponds to the aggregate current the branch is permitted to carry.
6	
7	The branch conductor 102 supplies a first connector station 110 and a second connector station 112. Two connector stations are shown for clarity of illustration. The system accommodates a larger plurality of connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each further connector station of the plurality. The branch conductor 102 also supplies a non-charging load 114, which is load connected to the same branch that is not under the control of the edge controller 100.
8	
9	A branch current sensor 104 measures total current on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector stations. Because the branch current sensor 104 is located upstream of those contactors, the current it measures includes both the current drawn by the connector stations and the current drawn by the non-charging load 114. The branch current sensor 104 is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured branch current to it.
10	
11	The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106. The isolated local bus 106 carries assigned current limits and contactor commands from the edge controller 100 to the connector stations, and carries connector current measurements and control-pilot status from the connector stations to the edge controller 100. The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the signalling electronics of each connector station.
12	
13	A network interface 108 connects the edge controller 100 to a remote management system. As described below, the network interface 108 conveys remote schedules and authorizations to the edge controller 100 and conveys uploaded meter records from the edge controller 100, but the safety behaviour of the system does not depend on the availability of the network interface 108.
14	
15	The connector station
16	
17	FIG. 2 shows the first connector station 110 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The first connector station 110 comprises a first contactor 120, a first connector current sensor 122, a first control-pilot interface 124, and a first vehicle connector 126. The first contactor 120 is connected in the power path between the branch conductor 102 and the first vehicle connector 126 and, when closed, permits current to flow from the branch conductor 102 to a vehicle coupled to the first vehicle connector 126. The first connector current sensor 122 measures the connector current flowing in that power path, that is, the current actually drawn by the vehicle coupled to the first vehicle connector 126.
18	
19	The first control-pilot interface 124 presents a control-pilot signal to the vehicle coupled to the first vehicle connector 126. The control-pilot signal advertises a maximum current, called here the assigned limit, that the vehicle is permitted to draw, and reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected and whether that vehicle is requesting energy. The first control-pilot interface 124 therefore serves both as the command path by which an assigned limit reaches the vehicle and as a status path by which the presence of a connected vehicle is reported to the edge controller 100.
20	
21	Each connector station of the plurality further has a local connector identifier. The local connector identifier is a stored value that distinguishes one connector of the plurality from another in the records, authorizations, and assignments held by the edge controller 100.
22	
23	The distinction between the first control-pilot interface 124 and the first connector current sensor 122 is used throughout this description. The first control-pilot interface 124 carries a command. The first connector current sensor 122 carries a measurement. The edge controller 100 does not treat the assigned limit sent through the first control-pilot interface 124 as evidence of the current that the connector is drawing. It obtains that evidence from the first connector current sensor 122.
24	
25	The edge controller
26	
27	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 100 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The edge controller 100 comprises a processing circuit 130 and a nonvolatile memory 132, and is coupled to the isolated local bus 106 and to the network interface 108. The processing circuit 130 executes the allocation and protection processes described below. The nonvolatile memory 132 retains stored values across loss of supply.
28	
29	The edge controller 100 further comprises a local fault indicator 134 and a service input 136. The local fault indicator 134 provides an indication at the equipment itself, independently of the network interface 108. The service input 136 is an input by which an installer places the edge controller 100 in a commissioning mode.
30	
31	For each active connector of the plurality, the edge controller 100 stores a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector is permitted to draw energy. The requested current is the current that the session would take if capacity were unconstrained. The minimum sustaining current is the smallest assigned limit at which the session at that connector is expected to remain charging rather than terminating and requiring a new start. 32	
33	Allocation at each allocation interval
34	
35	FIG. 4 shows the process carried out by the edge controller 100. The edge controller 100 repeats the allocation portion of the process at each allocation interval. The allocation interval is a recurring period at which the edge controller 100 revises the assigned limits.
36	
37	At an available-charging-current determination step 200, the edge controller 100 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. 39	At a minimum sustaining current assignment step 202, the edge controller 100 first assigns the minimum sustaining current to the sessions that can receive it. 41	At a deficit-based distribution step 204, the edge controller 100 distributes the remaining portion of the available charging current, that is, the portion left after the assignments made at the minimum sustaining current assignment step 202, according to energy deficit. 43	At a limit transmission and connector current verification step 206, the edge controller 100 sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector, and then verifies the resulting connector current with the connector current sensor of that connector. 54

A control-pilot command is advisory, and a vehicle that ignores it, responds too slowly, or responds only in coarse steps leaves the branch loaded above its limit. 58

62	
63	On reclosing, the edge controller 100 resumes the allocation interval process, and the reclosed session takes part in the assignments made at the minimum sustaining current assignment step 202 and the deficit-based distribution step 204 in the ordinary way.
64	
65	Welded-contactor isolation
66

70	
71	Operation during a network outage
72

74	
75	During a network outage the edge controller 100 continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process described above. 76	
77	Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory 132. The records accumulated during the outage are uploaded when communication returns.
78	
79	Installation mapping through the service input

86	
87	General considerations
88	
89	The allocation process, the branch protection process, the offline authorization behaviour, the welded-contactor isolation, and the installation mapping are described together because they share the sensors and the isolated local bus 106 of a single edge controller 100. 92	
93	The terms first and second are used to distinguish one connector station of the plurality from another and do not imply an order of importance or of operation. The system is not limited to two connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each connector station of the plurality. The embodiments described here are illustrative, and a person skilled in the art will recognize that elements described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with elements described in connection with another. The scope of the invention is defined by the claims that follow.

FIG. 1 shows a charging control system in which an edge controller 100 manages charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch. Supported and verified: edge controller 100, branch conductor 102, branch current sensor 104 upstream of the connector contactors, isolated local bus 106, network interface 108, connector stations 110/112 (contactor 120, connector current sensor 122, control-pilot interface 124, vehicle connector 126, local connector identifier), non-charging load 114, nonvolatile memory 132, local fault indicator 134, service input 136, and process steps 200-214; the per-connector stored quantities (authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy deficit); the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve arithmetic; minimum-sustaining-first then deficit-based distribution; pilot transmission with connector-current verification; the staged reduced-pilot / verification-interval / ordered one-at-a-time shedding sequence; the three reclose permissives including the randomized delay; welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and local fault annunciation; offline operation on a signed local token and last accepted branch limit; tamper-evident meter records uploaded on restoration; and low-energy pilot-transition installation mapping stored only on agreement. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md. Numerals are one-to-one with numerals.md, every figure numeral list matches its geometry, and no drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain. Untraced technical matter (critical): (1) FIG. 2 description states the control-pilot interface reports "whether that vehicle is requesting energy" — the source says only that it "reports a connected vehicle"; (2) the detailed description adds a sequential greedy rule for the minimum-sustaining pass ("takes the active connectors in turn ... for as long as the available charging current has not been exhausted", plus a definition of which session "cannot receive" it) that the source does not state; (3) claims 7 and 13 and the description place the tamper-evident meter-record sequence "in the nonvolatile memory", while the source recites nonvolatile memory only for the signed local token and the last accepted branch limit — this is an untraced dependent-claim limitation; (4) the description likewise places the shedding order and the commissioning association in nonvolatile memory 132, which the source does not say.

findings.title: Control-pilot interface said to report that the vehicle is "requesting energy" — no inventor support
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The connector station" section, paragraph beginning "The first control-pilot interface 124 presents a control-pilot signal"
findings.detail: The draft attributes a second status function to the control-pilot interface: reporting whether the coupled vehicle is requesting energy. The disclosure attributes exactly one status report to the control-pilot interface, namely that a vehicle is connected. No affirmative USER passage anywhere states that the pilot interface reports a request for energy; the stored "requested current" is a value the controller holds for each active connector, not a pilot-reported status. Vehicle-side pilot state signalling is common engineering knowledge, which is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected and whether that vehicle is requesting energy." Nearest source (disclosure.md / conversation.md USER): "A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired." The source never states that the interface reports a request for energy.
findings.fix: In that sentence, delete "and whether that vehicle is requesting energy" so it reads: "...and reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected."

findings.title: Sequential "in turn ... until exhausted" rule for the minimum-sustaining pass is not disclosed
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Allocation at each allocation interval" section, paragraph describing minimum sustaining current assignment step 202
findings.detail: The draft supplies a specific allocation algorithm — taking active connectors in turn and assigning until the available charging current is exhausted — and a specific definition of the session that "cannot receive" the minimum sustaining current. The disclosure states only the order of the two passes (minimum sustaining current first, then deficit-based distribution) and does not specify any sequence among connectors, any exhaustion condition, or any test for eligibility. This adds an operating rule of technical substance with no affirmative source passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The edge controller 100 takes the active connectors in turn and assigns the minimum sustaining current of each to that connector for as long as the available charging current has not been exhausted. A session for which a remaining part of the available charging current at that allocation interval is less than its minimum sustaining current is a session that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval." Nearest source: "It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." There is no source passage on connector order or exhaustion.
findings.fix: Replace both quoted sentences with: "The minimum sustaining current stored for each session that can receive it is assigned to that session before any further distribution of the available charging current is made."

findings.title: Claims 7 and 13 place the tamper-evident meter-record sequence in the nonvolatile memory — untraced claim limitation
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 7 and claim 13; draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Operation during a network outage" section, last paragraph
findings.detail: Two dependent claims and the description locate the tamper-evident meter-record sequence in the nonvolatile memory. The disclosure recites nonvolatile memory for exactly two items — the signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit — and describes the meter records only as appended to a "tamper-evident local sequence". A storage-location limitation of a dependent claim must trace to an affirmative source passage, and none exists.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 7): "to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory"; (claim 13): "appending meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory during the network outage"; (description): "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory 132." Nearest source: "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory" and, separately, "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns."
findings.fix: In claim 7 delete "in the nonvolatile memory" ("...to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence and to upload the appended meter records through the network interface when communication returns"). In claim 13 delete "in the nonvolatile memory" ("...appending meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence during the network outage and uploading..."). In the description, replace "held in the nonvolatile memory 132" with "held locally by the edge controller 100".

findings.title: Shedding order and commissioning association assigned to nonvolatile memory 132 without source support
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The shedding order is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132"; and "Installation mapping through the service input" section, paragraph beginning "The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor"
findings.detail: The draft assigns two further items to nonvolatile memory 132. The disclosure calls the shedding order "a stored shedding order" and says the mapping "is stored", without identifying the storage element; the only items the source places in nonvolatile memory are the signed local token and the last accepted branch limit. Assigning a specific storage element is a structural relationship that requires an affirmative source passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The shedding order is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 and defines the sequence in which the contactors ... are opened"; and "The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector." Nearest source: "the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order" and "The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector." Neither passage names nonvolatile memory.
findings.fix: Change the first sentence to "The shedding order is a stored value that defines the sequence in which the contactors of the plurality of connector stations are opened." Change the second to "The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector."

findings.title: Isolation boundary of the local bus specified as being at the connector-station signalling electronics
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Overview of the system" section, paragraph beginning "The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106"
findings.detail: The draft fixes where the isolation of the bus occurs — between the controller and the signalling electronics of each connector station. The disclosure says only that the controller "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus"; it identifies no isolation boundary and does not mention signalling electronics as a distinct element. This is a structural relationship with no affirmative source passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the signalling electronics of each connector station." Nearest source: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the connector stations."

findings.title: "Commissioning mode" construct is not in the source and is absent from the claims
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The edge controller" section (service input 136 paragraph), "Installation mapping through the service input" section, and "General considerations" section
findings.detail: The draft introduces an operating mode entered through the service input and then treats it as an omissible feature ("without the commissioning mode"). The disclosure describes the service input purely functionally: it permits an installer to carry out the mapping procedure. No source passage discloses a mode, a mode entry, or a mode-conditioned behaviour. Claim 8 correctly recites only "in response to the service input", so the description also departs from the claim terminology.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The service input 136 is an input by which an installer places the edge controller 100 in a commissioning mode"; "With the edge controller 100 in the commissioning mode entered through the service input 136, the edge controller 100 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time"; "without the commissioning mode". Nearest source: "A service input permits an installer to associate connector identifiers with physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the corresponding connector current sensor."
findings.fix: Change the first sentence to "The service input 136 is an input by which an installer initiates the association of connector identifiers with physical contactors described below." Change the second to "In response to the service input 136, the edge controller 100 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time...". In "General considerations", change "without the commissioning mode" to "without the installation mapping described above".

findings.title: Signed token said to identify authorized connectors by their local connector identifiers
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Operation during a network outage" section, paragraph beginning "The edge controller 100 stores a signed local authorization token"
findings.detail: The draft specifies the internal referencing mechanism of the token — that it names the connectors it authorizes by their local connector identifiers. The disclosure says only that the local token authorizes a connector and can expire, and separately that each connector has a local connector identifier; it never links the two. This is an added technical relationship without an affirmative source passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The signed local authorization token identifies the connectors it authorizes by their local connector identifiers and carries an expiry." Nearest source: "It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The signed local authorization token authorizes one or more connectors of the plurality and has an expiry."

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief provides no return path for the case the description says returns to the allocation process
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md geometry; draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph describing ordered contactor shedding step 210
findings.detail: The description states an outcome of step 210 in which the reduced pilot command has been effective and control returns to the allocation interval process. The FIG. 4 brief draws only one return line, and it leaves the reclose permissive step 212. There is therefore no depicted path corresponding to the effective-reduction branch, so the flow diagram and the description do not agree on the process the figure is said to show.
findings.evidence: Description: "If the measured branch current has fallen below the branch limit within the verification interval, the reduced pilot command has been effective and the edge controller 100 returns to the allocation interval process." FIG-4.md: the only return is "A return line leaves the left side of the reclose permissive step 212 ... and ends at the left side of the available-charging-current determination step 200"; the brief lists no other line leaving step 210 except the downward line to step 212 and the line to step 214.
findings.fix: Add to the FIG. 4 geometry, after the bullet describing the right-hand column: "A further return line leaves the left side of the ordered contactor shedding step 210, runs to the left clear of the left column, and joins the return line that ends at the left side of the available-charging-current determination step 200, so that the arrowhead at that rectangle serves both return lines."

findings.title: FIG. 3 omits the branch-current-sensor input that FIG. 1, the description, and claim 1 require
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md geometry; compare figures/FIG-1.md and draft/09-claims.md claim 1
findings.detail: FIG. 1 draws a connection from the branch current sensor 104 to the top edge of the edge controller 100 and states it is distinct from the isolated local bus 106; the description and claim 1 both recite that separate coupling. The enlarged view of the same controller in FIG. 3 shows the network interface, the isolated local bus, and the service input crossing the enclosing rectangle, but shows no branch-sensor input at all. The two views of the same part disagree about its connections.
findings.evidence: FIG-1.md: "A separate line runs from the branch current sensor 104 downward and to the left ... to the top edge of the edge controller 100. This line joins the branch current sensor 104 to the edge controller 100 and is distinct from the isolated local bus 106." Claim 1: "a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor". FIG-3.md geometry lists only rectangles 130, 132, 108, 134, 136 and the bus line; no branch-sensor connection appears.
findings.fix: Add to the FIG. 3 geometry: "A line enters the enclosing rectangle through its top side from a point well inside the upper part of the drawing area and runs to the top side of the processing circuit 130. This line is the connection from the branch current sensor 104 of FIG. 1 and is separate from the isolated local bus 106; no numeral is applied to it in this view." The numeral list for FIG. 3 is unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 2 leaves the incoming branch conductor unnumbered although it is numbered part 102
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md geometry and "Numerals shown on this figure" list
findings.detail: The line entering FIG. 2 and forming the power path is, per the description, the branch conductor 102 that feeds the first contactor 120. The brief directs that it be drawn as an unnumbered line, which conflicts with the like-reference-numerals convention recited at the head of the detailed description and with the description of the contactor's connection.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "A horizontal line enters the enclosing rectangle through its upper left side from a short unnumbered line at the upper left of the drawing area, and inside the enclosing rectangle forms the power path running to the right." Description: "The first contactor 120 is connected in the power path between the branch conductor 102 and the first vehicle connector 126." Detailed description opening: "Like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views."
findings.fix: Change the bullet to: "A horizontal line enters the enclosing rectangle through its upper left side from a short line at the upper left of the drawing area, that short line being the branch conductor 102, and inside the enclosing rectangle forms the power path running to the right." Add "- 102" to the FIG. 2 numeral list, and add a leader instruction: "For the branch conductor 102, end the leader on the portion of that line outside the enclosing rectangle."

findings.title: Claim 9 recites "each assigned limit" with no antecedent basis
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 9, the "sending each assigned limit" step
findings.detail: In claim 1 the term "assigned limit" is introduced in the connector-station element ("a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit"), so "each assigned limit" later in that claim has support. Claim 9 is independent and its preamble introduces only a contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a branch current sensor; no assigned limit is ever introduced before it is referred to as "each assigned limit".
findings.evidence: Claim 9: "...and then distributing a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values; sending each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding electric-vehicle connector...". Compare claim 1: "a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector".
findings.fix: In claim 9, amend the distribution step to end "...according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned limit for each of the active connectors;" and leave the following step as "sending each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding electric-vehicle connector and verifying a resulting connector current with the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector;".

structured_output.summary:
Ledger result: the great majority of the draft traces cleanly to the inventor text, but eleven items do not. Supported and verified: edge controller 100, branch conductor 102, branch current sensor 104 upstream of the connector contactors, isolated local bus 106, network interface 108, connector stations 110/112 (contactor 120, connector current sensor 122, control-pilot interface 124, vehicle connector 126, local connector identifier), non-charging load 114, nonvolatile memory 132, local fault indicator 134, service input 136, and process steps 200-214; the per-connector stored quantities (authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy deficit); the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve arithmetic; minimum-sustaining-first then deficit-based distribution; pilot transmission with connector-current verification; the staged reduced-pilot / verification-interval / ordered one-at-a-time shedding sequence; the three reclose permissives including the randomized delay; welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and local fault annunciation; offline operation on a signed local token and last accepted branch limit; tamper-evident meter records uploaded on restoration; and low-energy pilot-transition installation mapping stored only on agreement. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md. Numerals are one-to-one with numerals.md, every figure numeral list matches its geometry, and no drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain. There are no sectional views, so the section-line designation check is inapplicable (no resulting view, source-view brief, or drawing description recites a section line). Figure briefs keep shape choices as depiction conventions ("shown schematically", plain rectangles), the FIG. 2 series-order caveat stays confined to the brief, and no application text justifies a renderer's outline "by way of example" or as "any closed outline".

Untraced technical matter (critical): (1) FIG. 2 description states the control-pilot interface reports "whether that vehicle is requesting energy" — the source says only that it "reports a connected vehicle"; (2) the detailed description adds a sequential greedy rule for the minimum-sustaining pass ("takes the active connectors in turn ... for as long as the available charging current has not been exhausted", plus a definition of which session "cannot receive" it) that the source does not state; (3) claims 7 and 13 and the description place the tamper-evident meter-record sequence "in the nonvolatile memory", while the source recites nonvolatile memory only for the signed local token and the last accepted branch limit — this is an untraced dependent-claim limitation; (4) the description likewise places the shedding order and the commissioning association in nonvolatile memory 132, which the source does not say.

Further untraced items (major): (5) the description fixes the isolation boundary of the bus "between the edge controller 100 and the signalling electronics of each connector station"; (6) the description introduces a "commissioning mode" as the state entered through the service input, a construct absent from the source and from claim 8; (7) the description states that the signed token "identifies the connectors it authorizes by their local connector identifiers", a mechanism the source does not describe.

Internal consistency (minor): (8) paragraph 51 says the controller "returns to the allocation interval process" when the reduced pilot command was effective, but the FIG. 4 brief provides no return path from step 210 — the only return runs from step 212; (9) FIG. 1 and claim 1 show/recite a branch-current-sensor connection to the controller that is distinct from the isolated local bus, yet the enlarged FIG. 3 brief of that same controller omits any such input while showing every other external connection; (10) FIG. 2 draws the incoming supply line as "a short unnumbered line" although the description identifies that conductor as branch conductor 102, contrary to the like-numerals convention; (11) claim 9 recites "sending each assigned limit" with no antecedent for "assigned limit" (claim 1 introduces it in the connector-station element; claim 9's preamble does not).

Each finding below carries the candidate wording, the nearest source passage showing the gap, and a filing-clean automatic fix. No assessment of patentability, novelty, or scope quality is included, per the preflight's remit. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the disclosure, as instructed; they remain for the later prior-art review.

findings.title: Control-pilot interface said to report that the vehicle is "requesting energy" — no inventor support
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The connector station" section, paragraph beginning "The first control-pilot interface 124 presents a control-pilot signal"
findings.detail: The draft attributes a second status function to the control-pilot interface: reporting whether the coupled vehicle is requesting energy. The disclosure attributes exactly one status report to the control-pilot interface, namely that a vehicle is connected. No affirmative USER passage anywhere states that the pilot interface reports a request for energy; the stored "requested current" is a value the controller holds for each active connector, not a pilot-reported status. Vehicle-side pilot state signalling is common engineering knowledge, which is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected and whether that vehicle is requesting energy." Nearest source (disclosure.md / conversation.md USER): "A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired." The source never states that the interface reports a request for energy.
findings.fix: In that sentence, delete "and whether that vehicle is requesting energy" so it reads: "...and reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected."

findings.title: Sequential "in turn ... until exhausted" rule for the minimum-sustaining pass is not disclosed
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Allocation at each allocation interval" section, paragraph describing minimum sustaining current assignment step 202
findings.detail: The draft supplies a specific allocation algorithm — taking active connectors in turn and assigning until the available charging current is exhausted — and a specific definition of the session that "cannot receive" the minimum sustaining current. The disclosure states only the order of the two passes (minimum sustaining current first, then deficit-based distribution) and does not specify any sequence among connectors, any exhaustion condition, or any test for eligibility. This adds an operating rule of technical substance with no affirmative source passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The edge controller 100 takes the active connectors in turn and assigns the minimum sustaining current of each to that connector for as long as the available charging current has not been exhausted. A session for which a remaining part of the available charging current at that allocation interval is less than its minimum sustaining current is a session that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval." Nearest source: "It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." There is no source passage on connector order or exhaustion.
findings.fix: Replace both quoted sentences with: "The minimum sustaining current stored for each session that can receive it is assigned to that session before any further distribution of the available charging current is made."

findings.title: Claims 7 and 13 place the tamper-evident meter-record sequence in the nonvolatile memory — untraced claim limitation
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 7 and claim 13; draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Operation during a network outage" section, last paragraph
findings.detail: Two dependent claims and the description locate the tamper-evident meter-record sequence in the nonvolatile memory. The disclosure recites nonvolatile memory for exactly two items — the signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit — and describes the meter records only as appended to a "tamper-evident local sequence". A storage-location limitation of a dependent claim must trace to an affirmative source passage, and none exists.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 7): "to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory"; (claim 13): "appending meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory during the network outage"; (description): "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory 132." Nearest source: "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory" and, separately, "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns."
findings.fix: In claim 7 delete "in the nonvolatile memory" ("...to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence and to upload the appended meter records through the network interface when communication returns"). In claim 13 delete "in the nonvolatile memory" ("...appending meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence during the network outage and uploading..."). In the description, replace "held in the nonvolatile memory 132" with "held locally by the edge controller 100".

findings.title: Shedding order and commissioning association assigned to nonvolatile memory 132 without source support
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The shedding order is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132"; and "Installation mapping through the service input" section, paragraph beginning "The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor"
findings.detail: The draft assigns two further items to nonvolatile memory 132. The disclosure calls the shedding order "a stored shedding order" and says the mapping "is stored", without identifying the storage element; the only items the source places in nonvolatile memory are the signed local token and the last accepted branch limit. Neither passage names nonvolatile memory.

Change the second to "The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector."
